description:
The M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (MSAIE) offers concentrations in different engineering disciplines. It is for students with an undergraduate degree in engineering or a related field who are interested in a professional master’s degree to jumpstart a career in AI engineering.

The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers the Biomedical Engineering (BME) concentration of the MSAIE degree. In this concentration, students develop an AI specialty in the area of biomedical and healthcare applications. Artificial intelligence is already disrupting all areas of healthcare: medical imaging and diagnostics, electronic health records, drug discovery, and medical robotics. This trend is expected to grow in the future. The M.S. in AIE-BME program at CMU builds upon core strengths in engineering and computer science to develop leaders in the area of AI applications in healthcare. The graduates will be ideally positioned for successful careers in this rapidly growing field.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Biomedical Engineering

description: The M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (MSAIE) provides students with the knowledge and skills needed to engineer and develop AI systems, products, and services. The MSAIE requires a core curriculum in AI foundations and markets, plus specialized AI engineering coursework in a specific engineering discipline. Each engineering discipline offers one of two options: either a coursework-only option or a research option where students conduct original research with a faculty member. The degree requires a minimum of 11 courses and can be completed in 3 semesters.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Biomedical Engineering - Research

Concentration name: Bioimaging, Biomechanics and Medical Devices, Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology, Computational Biomedical Engineering
description: The M.S. program in biomedical engineering requires 96 units of coursework. It is designed to be completed in two semesters (fall and spring) of full-time study. The curriculum consists of biomedical engineering core courses, engineering/science elective courses, and a BME M.S. seminar course series. This curriculum provides M.S. students with the advanced skills necessary to be successful in industry or to be a competitive applicant for a top-tier Ph.D. program.

The Master of Science (M.S.) in Biomedical Engineering program provides students with the engineering and life science skills to succeed in careers in the biomedical engineering industry, academia or government, or to pursue further graduate studies in the field. The M.S. BME program emphasizes an in-depth, research-based educational experience that is tailored to each student’s career goals. Our focus on both engineering and biology from the molecular to the systems levels is a key feature of our program, as is our close collaboration with clinicians at local hospitals. This clinical collaboration opens up opportunities for our students to engage in translational research and to explore clinical applications of biomedical engineering. The department offers three options for completing the M.S. in Biomedical Engineering: the course-work option, the research-based option (thesis), and the applied study option (practicum). The applied study option is similar to the course-work option in most regards, except that students gain practical off-campus experience at a company site through a one-semester, full-time practicum.
Program name: M.S. in Biomedical Engineering - Applied Study

description: The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers a Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Engineering. The M.S. degree is earned by the successful completion of a minimum of 96 units of graduate-level coursework. The department’s graduate curriculum consists of core courses in biomedical engineering, a menu of advanced engineering and biology electives, free electives, and a seminar series. The core courses provide an advanced understanding of the fundamentals of biomedical engineering in the areas of physiology, biomaterials, bioinstrumentation, and cell and molecular biology. The advanced electives permit students to tailor their graduate education to match their research interests and career goals. Students also participate in a graduate seminar series, which exposes them to cutting-edge research through presentations from academic and industry leaders in biomedical engineering. The M.S. research option is a thesis-based degree that prepares students for R&D careers in industry or for Ph.D. studies in biomedical engineering or related fields. The research option requires a minimum of three semesters of full-time enrollment and provides students with an in-depth research experience that culminates in a master’s thesis.

The M.S. in Computational Biomedical Engineering program trains students to apply advanced computational techniques to solve problems in biology and medicine. This professional M.S. program is designed to be completed in two semesters of coursework with the option of a one-semester research project or a third semester of coursework. The curriculum is composed of courses from engineering, computer science, and biological sciences. The program culminates in a practicum course in which students work in teams to solve real-world problems in the biomedical industry. Students who successfully complete the program will be prepared to enter the biomedical industry in positions that require advanced computational skills. Examples of typical positions include data scientists in large medical centers, analysts in biotechnology companies, or developers of biomedical software.

The M.S. in Computational Biomedical Engineering (MS-CBME) trains students in the application of state-of-the-art computational approaches to solve problems in biology and medicine. The program provides the necessary depth and breadth of knowledge in biomedical engineering and computational sciences as well as hands-on experience in research and development. Students complete core competency courses to develop skills in computational modeling and data science as well as biomedical engineering application courses in areas such as neuroengineering, medical robotics, and cardiovascular engineering. The program culminates in a project in which students apply the learned skills to solve a substantial problem in a biomedical domain. The MS-CBME program is appropriate for students with undergraduate backgrounds in biomedical engineering or other engineering disciplines, as well as computer science, biology, chemistry, and physics, who may not have a traditional engineering background.
Program name: M.S. in Computational Biomedical Engineering - Applied Study

description: The M.S. in Computational Biomedical Engineering (MS-CBME) program provides cutting-edge training in the growing area of computational biomedical engineering. Students will be trained in applying engineering approaches to understand complex biological systems, and to develop computational models and platforms to solve biomedical problems. This program combines the strengths of the Biomedical Engineering and the Computational Biology departments. Students can choose to pursue either a research-intensive track or a professionally-oriented track. The research track will prepare students for careers in academic or industrial research and development. The applied track is intended for students who wish to pursue careers in industry. Both tracks will provide students with the fundamental knowledge and practical skills for addressing biomedical problems using computational approaches.
Program name: M.S. in Computational Biomedical Engineering - Research

Concentration name: Biomechanics and Mechanobiology Track, Biomaterials and Tissue Engineering Track, Computational Biomedical Engineering Track, Neuroengineering Track
description: The Ph.D. program in biomedical engineering requires a minimum of 96 units of coursework. In general, 36 units must consist of graduate courses in biomedical engineering, 24 units in an allied engineering or science field and 36 units in biomedical engineering research. The Ph.D. program is strongly research-oriented and requires a research specialty in one of the primary areas of the department faculty. After passing a qualifying examination, the student will pursue an individual research program under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Upon completion of the research, the student must submit a thesis based on this research and defend it in a a final oral examination.

The M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (MSAIE) is an interdepartmental degree program offered by the College of Engineering. This catalog page covers the MSAIE degree with a concentration in Chemical Engineering (MSAIE-ChemE). Today's engineers are expected to be experts in their own discipline and also to be proficient at using computer hardware, software and the network to design, analyze, and deploy complex systems. With the rising prominence of artificial intelligence, a new generation of engineers will need to also be proficient in using AI to build and analyze autonomous and intelligent engineering systems. The College of Engineering at Carnegie Mellon is meeting this need with a new master’s degree in Artificial Intelligence Engineering that will train students to innovate and develop solutions in this emerging field. The curriculum will provide students with a strong foundation in both the engineering and AI domains. Students will develop their knowledge of AI principles, models, and methods to conceptualize, design, and validate engineering systems that require the integration of AI components and analysis. Upon completion of the degree, graduates will have the unique skills to design, develop and deploy AI solutions for engineering applications.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Chemical Engineering

description: The department offers a coursework-only M.S. degree and a research-based M.S. degree. Students in the coursework option choose from the following tracks: general chemical engineering, data analytics and machine learning, materials, and risk management. The coursework-only M.S. option does not require a thesis or research project. Students in this option select one of four areas of concentration, each of which require a specific set of coursework. The research-based M.S. option requires students to complete a research project and associated M.S. thesis in addition to coursework. All M.S. students must successfully complete 96 units of graduate coursework.

The M.S. degree in Chemical Engineering is awarded after the satisfactory completion of an approved program of study, which consists of at least 96 units of coursework, a research project (at least 36 units) and a final report on this project. This report should be of a quality suitable for publication. All M.S. candidates must pass the M.S. Seminar course (06-800).

The one-year Applied Study M.S. degree is a professional degree that provides students with hands-on, industry-oriented experiences while training them in the foundational principles of chemical engineering. This degree is designed to prepare students for careers in chemical process and related industries. The program builds on the fundamentals of chemical engineering with advanced coursework in transport phenomena, thermodynamics, and reaction kinetics, as well as exposure to chemical process systems engineering. Graduates from the Applied Study program will have an in-depth knowledge of chemical engineering principles and practices and be skilled in process modeling. Students can select their coursework electives to focus on a particular area, such as process systems engineering, energy, environmental engineering, colloids and nanomaterials, or polymers.
Program name: M.S. in Chemical Engineering - Applied Study

description: The graduate program in the Department of Chemical Engineering provides students with an opportunity to make an important and lasting contribution to the field of chemical engineering. Students may obtain a Ph.D. or M.S. degree. Students are typically admitted directly into the Ph.D. program; however, under special circumstances, a student may be admitted into a terminal M.S. program. The graduate curriculum provides the student with an advanced knowledge of the fundamentals of chemical engineering. Students may also obtain in-depth knowledge in a particular area of specialization by selecting an appropriate set of elective courses. The elective courses are offered by various departments at Carnegie Mellon University. Through their research, students become part of the research culture in the department where collaboration among different research groups is common. The graduate program provides a rich and stimulating environment for learning, research and personal growth. The program is flexible and can be adapted to the interests of the individual student. A major component of the graduate curriculum is training in research. The graduate students and faculty in the department are engaged in research projects in the following areas: Advanced materials and nanotechnology; Biological and biomedical engineering; Complex fluids engineering; Energy and the environment; and Process systems engineering. A detailed listing of the various research projects is available at the department website. Students can tailor a sequence of courses and a research topic that satisfy their own goals.

The M.S. in Advanced Infrastructure Systems (AIS) is a nine-month, 96-unit professional master’s degree program designed for students with an undergraduate degree in a relevant engineering discipline or a quantitative background in science, economics, or a related field. The program is structured to allow students to pursue areas of interest by selecting courses from a variety of technical focus areas in CEE and other departments at Carnegie Mellon. The four technical areas are: Sensing and Data Analytics; Control and Optimization; Mechanics, Materials, and Computing; and Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, and Science. Infrastructure systems are increasingly complex, consisting of an extensive network of interdependent physical and cyber components. At the same time, new sensing, communication, and computing technologies are revolutionizing how we monitor, control, and operate infrastructure. The AIS M.S. program provides students with the tools to apply the latest technology in sensing, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to build, manage, and operate the next generation of smart and resilient civil and environmental infrastructure systems. Students may choose to focus their studies on topics such as intelligent transportation systems, smart buildings, sustainable energy systems, and resilient water systems. Graduates of the program are ideally suited for jobs with technology companies developing solutions for infrastructure systems, consulting firms working on infrastructure challenges, and public agencies responsible for infrastructure planning and management. Students complete a rigorous curriculum that consists of a set of core courses and a suite of technical electives, as well as a significant project course where they work in teams to solve a real-world problem. The curriculum provides both breadth and depth in the latest methods and tools for developing and managing smart and resilient infrastructure systems, so that graduates are qualified to lead in this rapidly-evolving field.

The College of Engineering offers a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (MS AIE) with a concentration in Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE). The MS AIE-CEE degree provides education in theory and practice on the application of AI and machine learning to civil and environmental engineering problems. Students will learn the fundamentals of AI/ML through a core set of courses and apply this knowledge to a broad range of civil and environmental engineering challenges through core and elective courses in CEE. Students entering the MS AIE-CEE degree will have a strong undergraduate education in engineering. Students will be required to take a set of core courses offered by various departments in the college of engineering, and a set of core and elective courses offered by CEE. This degree combines the strengths of CEE at CMU, ranked in the top 10 by US News and World Report, and CMU’s College of Engineering which is a global leader in engineering education and research with a growing strength in AI/ML through its new AI initiative.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Civil and Environmental Engineering

description: The M.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering is a course-work based M.S. degree. A total of 96 units of coursework are required for the degree. This includes 60 units of coursework from the CEE department, of which at least 36 units must be from one of the primary CEE focus areas (see list below). The remaining 36 units of coursework are free electives that may be selected from any graduate program at CMU. There is no research or project requirement. The course-only M.S. degree can be completed in two semesters of full-time study.

The M.S. in Civil and Computer Engineering (M.S.-CCE) is an interdepartmental program between Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) and Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE). The degree is for students who want a master’s degree that combines the skillsets of both of these engineering disciplines to develop and deploy solutions for smart cities and resilient infrastructure systems. This includes areas such as smart infrastructure sensing and control, intelligent transportation systems, energy systems and buildings, and water systems. M.S.-CCE students obtain a deep understanding of cyber-physical systems and learn skills in sensing, communication, data analytics, and control. They become proficient in using these skills to design, build, and operate smart civil infrastructure systems. The program provides the foundational knowledge and specialized skills for students to enter the workforce or for more advanced graduate studies. Upon completion of the program, students will earn an M.S. in Civil and Computer Engineering.
Program name: M.S. in Civil and Computer Engineering

Concentration name: Advanced Infrastructure Systems (AIS); Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, and Science (EESS); Mechanics, Materials, and Computing (MMC)
description: The M.S. program in Civil and Environmental Engineering provides students with the fundamental principles of engineering and the skills needed to address the grand challenges of our time. The curriculum offers flexibility and choice in coursework, as well as several paths to complete the degree. The M.S. program can be pursued with a research or professional focus. The research-focused M.S. involves in-depth study with a faculty advisor on a research topic that is presented in a master’s thesis. The professional M.S. is a coursework-based degree that can be completed on an accelerated timeline. Students in the M.S. program without a specialized degree designation can pursue coursework and research in one of the following areas: Advanced Infrastructure Systems (AIS); Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, and Science (EESS); or Mechanics, Materials, and Computing (MMC). For detailed program information and degree requirements, please see the CEE graduate student handbook.
Program name: M.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering

description: The M.S. in CEE-Applied Study is for students who wish to pursue a CEE masters-level education, with a strong emphasis on professional development. It has the same core course requirements as the traditional M.S. in CEE but replaces the technical elective requirement with a required, immersive CEE-related internship. The Applied Study internship provides opportunities for students to learn from and contribute to industry or government organizations where they can apply knowledge and skills learned in the CEE graduate curriculum, and also to learn about new technologies, applications, and professional practices. CEE-Applied Study students may focus their program of study in any of CEE’s graduate study areas: Advanced Infrastructure Systems (AIS); Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, and Science (EESS); or Mechanics, Materials, and Computing (MMC). Students successfully completing an internship through the Applied Study program also complete a written report and give an oral presentation describing and reflecting on their internship experiences.
Program name: M.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering - Applied Study

description: The M.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering program is designed to provide students with the fundamentals of their chosen area of specialization as well as the breadth of knowledge required to work with other specialists in their profession. M.S. students specialize in one of the following areas: Advanced Infrastructure Systems (AIS); Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, and Science (EESS); or Mechanics, Materials, and Computing (MMC). Students may choose between a coursework-only option or a research option. The research option M.S. program is for students interested in a research-focused degree. The program takes approximately three to four semesters to complete. Students are required to take 96 units of coursework (typically 8 courses) and complete a research thesis for 24-36 units.
Program name: M.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering - Research

description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree is conferred upon a student who has demonstrated a high level of ability in a specific field of knowledge. In the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department, this is interpreted to mean that the successful candidate has performed original research of high quality in a particular sub-area of civil and environmental engineering. The Ph.D. degree is primarily a research degree. While a required number of course credits must be completed, the main requirement is the completion of a dissertation that is judged by the faculty to be an original and significant contribution to the field. Students typically select one of three major areas of study: Advanced Infrastructure Systems (AIS); Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, and Science (EESS); or Mechanics, Materials, and Computing (MMC). Additional information can be obtained by contacting the CEE Graduate Coordinator or by visiting the departmental website.
Program name: Ph.D. in Civil and Environmental Engineering

description:
The M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Electrical and Computer Engineering (MS-AIE-ECE) is for students who wish to pursue a master's degree in Artificial Intelligence (AI) Engineering with a focus on the ECE aspects of AI. The degree provides students with a strong foundation in AI techniques as well as the underlying ECE principles, such as computer hardware for AI, so they may engineer a wide range of AI systems. The MS-AIE-ECE degree is intended to be a terminal professional master’s degree for students who are not planning to pursue a Ph.D. in the future. The program provides an education in the principles and practice of AI Engineering for students who have a bachelor’s degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering or a related field. The ECE core AI courses cover the foundations of machine learning and deep learning, while also allowing students to take advanced electives to specialize further in their areas of interest. In addition, the program requires coursework in engineering hardware for AI, in particular courses in computer architecture and digital VLSI design which provide the foundation for hardware accelerators for AI.

The degree requires a practicum in which students gain experience in building AI systems. Students can fulfill this requirement by taking an existing course, 18-662 (Introduction to Deep Learning), or by taking a project course. Graduates of the program will have a wide variety of career opportunities, such as Machine Learning Engineer, Deep Learning Engineer, and AI Systems Engineer; and graduates of the program will be well-positioned for such roles.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Electrical and Computer Engineering

Concentration name: Computer Security, Cyber-Physical Systems, Data and Network Science, Hardware Systems, Integrated Systems Design, Mobile and IoT Engineering, Signal, Image, and Data Processing, Software Systems
description: The M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) program is a coursework-only master's degree that prepares students for an exciting, productive, and rewarding career in engineering. This professional degree is designed for students who want to enter the industry with a solid foundation of ECE fundamentals coupled with a specialized coursework focus. The M.S. in ECE program can also serve as a good entry point to the Ph.D. program for students who would like to get a glimpse into the Ph.D. program without having to commit to it upfront. Students in the M.S. in ECE program may apply to the Ph.D. program in ECE in their second semester.
Program name: M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering

description: The Ph.D. program in ECE is an internationally-recognized, research-intensive program designed to develop the next generation of faculty, industry, and government leaders. The Ph.D. is the highest degree offered by the department. Students pursue in-depth studies in a major area and conduct original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. The research areas of the department include: computer security, cyber-physical systems, machine learning and signal processing, data storage systems, computer architecture, integrated systems design and electronic design automation (CAD), applied electromagnetics and RF circuits, biomedical devices and MEMS, optics and photonics, networking, and software systems and mobile computing.
Program name: Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering

description: The M.S. in Engineering and Public Policy (EPP) is a research-based degree that prepares students for Ph.D. programs or for research-related careers in industry, government, or NGOs. Students take advanced classes in EPP and in another engineering or science discipline and pursue an interdisciplinary research thesis supervised by a faculty member in E.P.P. and in the partnering engineering or science discipline. This is a STEM-designated program. The M.S. in EPP is targeted at students with a bachelor’s degree in engineering or a science field. In their first semester, students identify a faculty advisor, an appropriate department in engineering or science that best supports their research interest, and a basic research plan for their master’s thesis. Students in the M.S. program will work with an advisor from the EPP department as well as an advisor from a collaborating department. Students will typically take two EPP courses (19-701 Intro to EPP and 19-702 Quantitative Methods in EPP), 3-4 other graduate-level courses to prepare for research in their chosen field, and 3-4 semesters of M.S. thesis research credit. A research thesis is a primary requirement for the degree. Students are typically full-time and self-supported for this degree. They can generally complete the program in three to four semesters. Students interested in the M.S. in EPP should specify this degree in their online application and indicate their research interests and EPP faculty of interest in their statement of purpose. Those interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in EPP should apply directly to the Ph.D. program.
Program name: M.S. in Engineering and Public Policy

description: The Ph.D. in Engineering and Public Policy (EPP) is a research-based degree for students who wish to work on problems at the intersection of technology and society. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, research-oriented positions in government and industry, and a variety of other public and private sector positions that require a deep understanding of both the technical and social dimensions of complex problems. The intellectual core of EPP is a problem-solving orientation that integrates engineering and social science. EPP Ph.D. students take courses and conduct research that joins a deep understanding of some area of engineering with the theories and methods of the social sciences. Students are expected to demonstrate through their research that they can frame a problem so that it can be understood by both engineers and social scientists, can choose and use the most appropriate analytical tools from both domains to address the problem, and can develop and communicate a solution that is both technically and socially sound. EPP faculty and students work on a diverse range of topics, including energy and environmental systems; risk analysis and communication; technology innovation and R&D policy; and information and communication technology policy. In addition to EPP faculty, many faculty in engineering, the social sciences, and other disciplines at Carnegie Mellon are affiliated with the department and are available to advise Ph.D. students. The EPP Ph.D. curriculum is highly flexible. Students work with their advisors to develop an individualized study plan that supports their research and career goals. All students must demonstrate a fundamental understanding of engineering, social science, and the tools of policy analysis. All students also take a two-semester sequence of project courses where they work in teams on real-world policy problems. Students typically complete the majority of their coursework in the first two years of the program. They also begin to work on research during their first year. By the end of the second year, students take a qualifying examination based on a research paper they have written. After passing the qualifier, students work on their Ph.D. dissertation. Students are expected to complete the dissertation within five years of entering the program. In addition to the departmental requirements, students must satisfy all of the requirements of the College of Engineering. Additional details on the curriculum, departmental requirements, and the research interests of EPP faculty and students can be found on the department web site. Most students entering the Ph.D. program have an undergraduate degree in some field of engineering, but students with strong backgrounds in science, mathematics, and other relevant fields are also admitted. Students with a relevant master’s degree are also welcome to apply. All full-time Ph.D. students are supported with a stipend and tuition.
Program name: Ph.D. in Engineering and Public Policy

Concentration name: software engineering, data science, information security, and network engineering
description: The Information and Communication Technology (ICT) M.S. program is offered exclusively at the Carnegie Mellon University Africa location. This program prepares the next generation of ICT leaders in Africa. The ICT M.S. degree provides an advanced professional and technical education in information and communication technology. Students learn to apply the technical skills acquired to make a significant impact in the digitization of Africa. Students develop breadth in technology and business and depth in a specific technical area that reflects their interests. The technical core includes courses in software development, networks and telecommunications, and data analytics. Students gain expertise in a chosen concentration area, which include software engineering, data science, information security, and network engineering.
Program name: M.S. in Information and Communication Technology

description: The Master of Science in Information Networking (MSIN) program is a specialized master's degree program for technical professionals who wish to gain expertise in the principles and practice of information networking. The program's core courses provide a strong foundation in the fundamentals of information networking, including network programming, data analytics, systems, and security. Through a variety of concentration courses, students can tailor the MSIN program to their specific interests, gaining knowledge in areas such as mobility, security, data analytics, network engineering and management, product management, and software development. The MSIN program's coursework provides a solid theoretical underpinning, while the curriculum's project-oriented courses offer students opportunities to apply their knowledge to solve real-world problems. By providing a combination of rigorous technical coursework and practical, industry-oriented training, the MSIN program prepares students for a variety of roles in industry and government.

The Information Networking Institute (INI) offers a doctoral degree, a Ph.D. in Information Networking. The INI is a unique interdisciplinary research and education institute that brings together faculty and students from across Carnegie Mellon University. The primary goal of the Ph.D. in INI program is to prepare students for a research career in academia or industry. Students in this program will pursue a research-focused curriculum, leading to the doctoral dissertation, in the fields of networking, security, mobile and wireless systems, and related areas. Our Ph.D. students work with world-class faculty in various departments at CMU. The Ph.D. in INI is offered as a Carnegie Mellon-wide interdisciplinary degree.

The College of Engineering will offer a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (MS AIE). This degree will provide students with the knowledge and skills to be leaders in AI engineering. It will provide a foundational knowledge in AI as well as depth in a chosen engineering discipline. The MS AIE program will provide training for a career in AI engineering in a wide variety of industries. The AI engineering focus provides differentiation from computer science degrees in AI or machine learning.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Materials Science and Engineering

description: The M.S. program is designed for individuals who wish to pursue a career as a practicing engineer or to pursue further graduate work. It is also suitable for individuals already in the workforce who wish to advance their knowledge. The program typically takes one year to complete and requires 96 units of coursework (typically 8 courses) at the graduate level, of which 48 units must be from courses offered by the Department of Materials Science and Engineering.
Program name: M.S. in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The Ph.D. degree is a research-oriented degree intended to prepare students for a career in research and/or academia. The department’s graduate program provides a core curriculum that develops a fundamental understanding of the structure, processing, properties and performance of materials while allowing the flexibility to pursue individual research interests. Our students select their own research topic and faculty advisor and are engaged in research within their first year in the program. Students can pursue research projects advised by any of the MSE faculty including our affiliated faculty in other departments. Coursework is determined on an individual basis with the student’s advisor and thesis committee. Ph.D. students are typically supported with a fellowship that covers tuition, fees and a stipend for living expenses. Requirements for the Ph.D. degree are successful completion of the Core Courses, an oral qualifying examination, a thesis proposal, and a final thesis defense. Details can be found in the MSE Graduate Student Handbook (https://www.cmu.edu/mse/graduate/current-students/phd-handbook.html).
Program name: Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The College of Engineering offers a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence Engineering with a concentration in Mechanical Engineering (MS AIE-ME). This program addresses the growing demand for AI specialists with a background in mechanical engineering. Students build upon a strong foundation in mechanical engineering with advanced coursework in AI fundamentals and applications. Students select from a range of courses in machine learning, computer vision, and robotics, and may also complete an optional practicum or research experience. The MS AIE-ME is a professional master's program that provides graduates with the skills and knowledge to solve complex engineering problems using AI. It is intended for students who have an undergraduate degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Mechanical Engineering

description: The M.S. degree is primarily intended for students who have completed a B.S. in mechanical engineering or a closely related field and wish to pursue a graduate degree. The program provides students with a solid and broad-based graduate education that can prepare them for a wide variety of career paths in industry, government, and academia. A central feature is the required coursework, which provides depth in the discipline and training outside the discipline. The M.S. degree has options for completing either a research or a practicum experience. The program is specifically designed to provide a graduate-level education for individuals pursuing a technical career in the mechanical engineering profession. The core of the program is an integrated set of courses in mathematics, science, and engineering. Students will gain experience with advanced engineering tools and will develop their ability to solve complex engineering problems and to communicate the results of their work effectively. For most students, the educational objectives will be aligned with the same objectives defined for the undergraduate degree in mechanical engineering from Carnegie Mellon.

The objective of the Ph.D. program in Mechanical Engineering is to produce a graduate who can define a research problem, design a program of study to solve the problem, and create new knowledge of a fundamental nature that is publishable in the archival literature of his or her field. As such, the doctorate is a research-oriented degree. The requirements for the degree are established with the goal of preventing over-specialization, yet assuring a thorough grounding in the fundamental principles of science and engineering. To satisfy the requirements, the student must have a bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, or mathematics. Normally, Ph.D. students will have already completed a master's degree in a related field. Students may also enter the Ph.D. program directly from the bachelor’s degree level if they have demonstrated exceptional ability and aptitude for research. A description of the research in the department is available on the Mechanical Engineering website.

The M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Energy Science, Technology & Policy (AIE-EST&P) is a professional master’s degree that combines an M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering focusing on Artificial Intelligence with an M.S. in Engineering & Technology Innovation Management with a focus in Energy. AIE-EST&P provides a unique educational opportunity for students to gain depth in AI engineering methods as well as a broad understanding of the interdisciplinary aspects of energy systems including technology, policy, and innovation management. The degree is administered by the College of Engineering's Information and Communication Technologies Institute and the Department of Engineering and Public Policy, which also works closely with the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation. Graduates will be prepared to take on high-impact roles at the forefront of the AI-energy revolution. Students pursuing the AIE-EST&P track are strongly encouraged to visit the EST&P website for additional information.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Energy Science, Technology & Policy

Concentration name: Energy Science, Technology & Policy - Applied Study
description: The M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering – Energy Science, Technology & Policy - Applied Study (AIE-EST&P-AS) is an interdisciplinary engineering master's degree that takes a holistic approach to energy through its world-class professional master’s program. We combine our expertise in technology with a deep understanding of the policy and business factors that shape energy systems and the environment. This Applied Study option is available for EST&P students who enroll in the AIE concentration to complete an industry internship or other practical experience in lieu of the traditional project course. Offered through the College of Engineering, AIE-EST&P provides students the opportunity to create an energy program tailored to their career goals through selection of an AIE concentration and a breadth of energy-related electives across CMU.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Energy Science, Technology & Policy - Applied Study

description:
The M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy (EST&P) is an interdisciplinary, engineering-centric master’s program at Carnegie Mellon University, with a purposeful blend of engineering, economics and public policy. EST&P is for students with an undergraduate degree in engineering or a related STEM field who want to be energy leaders of the future by gaining a deep understanding of the interdisciplinary aspects of the energy system. Graduates are prepared for careers that span the energy sector in industry, government, non-profits and academia, with diverse roles in research, development, and consulting.

EST&P is a 12-month program beginning in the fall semester, and coursework is completed in two semesters (fall and spring). In the summer semester, students can choose to do a project, an internship or take additional coursework to satisfy graduation requirements.

All students in the program gain a solid foundation in the fundamentals of energy, through core courses covering the modern energy system, energy conversion and supply, energy demand and utilization, and energy economics, policy and regulation.

To gain the necessary depth, students select an engineering concentration to focus their coursework. The concentration consists of three graduate-level engineering courses in a single area of focus from any of the engineering departments within the College of Engineering. In addition, students take one breadth elective course from any graduate program at CMU to broaden their perspective.
Program name: M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy

Concentration name: Chemical Engineering, Civil & Environmental Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, General
description:
The M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy - Advanced Study (EST&P-AS) is an engineering-focused master's degree for students who have an undergraduate engineering or science degree from CMU. The EST&P-AS program is a coursework-only degree that allows a student to graduate with both a B.S. and M.S. degree in as little as nine semesters.
The curriculum provides an in-depth study of a chosen engineering concentration:
Chemical Engineering
Civil & Environmental Engineering
Electrical & Computer Engineering
Materials Science & Engineering
Mechanical Engineering
A General track is also available for those with a non-traditional engineering or science background, but who meet the admissions requirements. This option allows students to design a curriculum by selecting courses from across all of the participating engineering departments.
The engineering concentration is combined with a breadth of courses in energy offered by faculty from across the College of Engineering.
This degree is only available to currently enrolled Carnegie Mellon undergraduate students.
Program name: M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy - Advanced Study

description:
The M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy (EST&P) is an engineering-focused, interdisciplinary master’s program at Carnegie Mellon University, offered jointly by the College of Engineering and the Wilton E. Scott Institute for Energy Innovation. The EST&P curriculum provides an in-depth, multi-faceted education in the field of energy. Students learn to frame, analyze, and solve the multi-dimensional challenges of the energy system. The curriculum includes core courses, depth courses, breadth courses, and a required internship or research project.
The Applied Study program is an option for students from our partner universities for whom an EST&P degree is part of an accelerated, combined, or dual-degree program with their home university. This program follows the curriculum of the professional M.S. track. EST&P students completing the Applied Study option satisfy the core course requirements and the College of Engineering’s breadth requirement.
Program name: M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy - Applied Study

description: The M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy – Applied Study (EST&P–AS) degree is completed in 16 months of full-time study, which includes a required internship during the summer between the first and second years. EST&P–AS students participate in the same breadth coursework as those in the Professional M.S. program, including the Energy Systems Core Courses and the Energy Policy, Economics, and Elective Courses. EST&P–AS students also receive hands-on training via labs and projects integrated in core courses, as well as have the option to pursue research through additional project-based coursework. The combination of comprehensive knowledge, advanced problem-solving skills and hands-on experience prepares EST&P-AS students to take leadership roles in the rapidly growing energy sector.
Program name: M.S. in Energy Science, Technology and Policy - Applied Advanced Study

description: The Artificial Intelligence Engineering-Engineering & Technology Innovation Management (AIE-ETIM) M.S. program is an integrated program offered by the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) and the Engineering & Technology Innovation Management (E&TIM) program. E&TIM is a program of Carnegie Mellon's College of Engineering, administered through the Carnegie Mellon University Integrated Innovation Institute. The AIE-ETIM program combines ECE's world-class artificial intelligence engineering curriculum with E&TIM's expertise and coursework in technology innovation management. The program is designed for students who want to develop cutting-edge AI skills and gain expertise in business and management so they can lead and manage complex technology projects. The students will learn AI techniques and their engineering applications and how to effectively manage innovation for a sustainable competitive advantage. Graduates of this integrated program will have the unique skills to become the future leaders in AI-related industries.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - Engineering & Technology Innovation Management

description: The Master of Science in Engineering & Technology Innovation Management (E&TIM) is a professional master's degree for candidates with a B.S. in engineering or science who want to make a career in the exciting domain of technology innovation. Offered as a one-year, two-semester program in Pittsburgh, E&TIM students build upon their technical backgrounds by adding the management skills necessary for leading a company's technical innovation with a business mindset. The degree is distinguished by its focus on technology innovation, its business and management curriculum that builds on a student's technical core and the required 8-12 week summer internship. It gives students the knowledge and skillsets to manage the entire technology commercialization process, from understanding a market opportunity, to research and development, to the protection of intellectual property, to developing a business plan and launching a product. The E&TIM degree culminates in an integrative capstone project in the spring where student teams work with a real-world company to help them commercialize their technology.
Program name: M.S. in Engineering and Technology Innovation Management

description: CMU’s Master of Architecture (M.Arch) is an NAAB-accredited professional degree program that prepares students to become licensed architects. The M.Arch program provides a rigorous, in-depth, and holistic architectural education that integrates design excellence with critical inquiry and technological innovation. The program foregrounds social equity, environmental justice, and climate action in order to build a better world. The M.Arch program emphasizes the role of the architect in the complex socio-technical and environmental systems in which they operate. Through project-based learning, students work on real-world problems and develop skills in collaboration, creativity, and critical thinking. The program culminates in a graduate thesis that allows students to focus their design research in an area of their choosing. Students in our M.Arch program become part of a vibrant, inclusive community of faculty, staff, students, and alumni. Through dedicated advising, mentorship programs, and a host of student groups, our students are supported in their educational journey and prepared for successful careers in architecture and related fields. We leverage our location in Pittsburgh to connect with communities and engage in hands-on, place-based learning.

The Master of Science in Architecture (MS in Arch) is a non-accredited, two-semester degree for students with an undergraduate professional degree in architecture or a closely related field. The primary purpose of the MS in Arch is to offer in-depth knowledge and specialization in architecture in preparation for a career in research, teaching or specialized practice. Specialization is pursued through a focused curriculum and the development of a master's thesis in the second semester. Thesis topics are proposed by the students according to their interests and are pursued with the guidance of a faculty advisor. The thesis typically takes the form of a major research paper that is documented in a bound volume and presented to the faculty at the end of the spring semester.

The MS in Architecture is a research-based STEM degree as defined by the Department of Homeland Security.

For more information, please visit the School of Architecture website.

The Master of Science in Building Performance and Diagnostics (MSBPD) is a research-based master's degree that prepares students for positions in research and consulting in the building industry, for positions in the development of building products and systems, and for the pursuit of a Ph.D. in building science. The program addresses the need for a new generation of professionals with the integrated knowledge and skills to create high-performance buildings and cities. High-performance buildings are those that are sustainable—in their use of energy, water and materials—as well as healthy, comfortable and productive for their occupants. The program educates students in the fundamental scientific principles and analytical methods of building science, with a primary focus on energy use, environmental performance and occupant comfort. Students develop expertise in a variety of specialty areas, including: advanced building systems integration and diagnostics; building controls and automation; and computational modeling and simulation of building performance. The MSBPD program requires two semesters of core courses and one semester to complete a research-based master's thesis. In the first year, core courses include: fundamentals of building performance; commercial building performance and diagnostics; advanced building systems integration and diagnostics; and a building performance modeling seminar.
Program name: M.S. in Building Performance and Diagnostics

description:
The Master of Science in Computational Design (MSCD) is a research-based master’s program that provides a foundation in the theory, methods, and technologies of computational design, and an opportunity for specialization through project-based learning. As a STEM-designated degree, the MSCD prepares students for careers in computational design research and development in academia, industry, and the creative professions.

Students in the MSCD program draw on a rich interdisciplinary environment. Computational design faculty collaborate across the university with the departments of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and the School of Computer Science, including the Human-Computer Interaction Institute, the Robotics Institute, and the Institute for Software Research. Students may also engage with research centers across campus, including the Center for Building Performance and Diagnostics, the Remaking Cities Institute, the Frank-Ratchye STUDIO for Creative Inquiry, and the Entertainment Technology Center.

CMU's Master of Science in Computational Design program prepares students to:

Develop advanced knowledge and skills in computational design thinking, methods, and making.
Conduct design-led, project-based research in a specialized area of computational design.
Define and pursue an original inquiry that makes a substantial contribution to the field.
Communicate complex concepts and project work in a clear and compelling way.

Students in the MSCD program focus their studies through project-based research in one of the school’s computational design research labs. Current labs include:

Advanced anufacturing and materials research within the Scibotics Lab
Artificial intelligence in architecture within the CoDe Lab
Design for the environment within the Resilient Buildings Lab
Performance-based modeling and simulation with the Center for Building Performance and Diagnostics
Generative and parametric design within the Design Fabrication Lab
Robotics and human-machine interaction within the RoBotS Lab

The MSCD is a two-year (four-semester) degree for students with a background in design, architecture, engineering, computer science, or a related field, who want to conduct research in computational design. Prospective students should apply directly to the MSCD program.

The Master of Science in Sustainable Design (MSSD) is an advanced, post-professional research-based degree program that prepares students for careers in sustainable architecture and design in the built environment. It is a STEM-designated degree program (CIP Code 04.0902).

The degree attracts students from a wide variety of backgrounds, both in terms of disciplines of study and cultural heritages. The primary constituencies from which students are drawn include: junior and mid-career professionals in architecture and other building industry disciplines who seek to deepen and focus their knowledge in sustainability; students matriculating from pre-professional undergraduate programs in architecture, engineering and related disciplines; and international students with academic backgrounds in architecture and other building-related disciplines who have practiced or wish to practice in an international arena.

The goal of the MSSD is to create leaders who will drive innovation in design, technology and policy for a sustainable built environment. The curriculum focuses on both breadth and depth of knowledge in sustainability. It leverages the technical and design strengths of the School of Architecture to create an integrated understanding of building science and technology with design thinking. A strong grounding in fundamental and advanced concepts in building physics, building performance simulation and data analytics, environmental material systems, and design strategies is complemented with in-depth study of a wide variety of advanced topics. The program is flexible to accommodate students with different backgrounds and experience levels. After an initial semester that establishes foundational knowledge and skills, students define a specialized area of study under the guidance of the faculty. The program culminates in a final research or design thesis project that contributes to the knowledge base of sustainable design and architecture.

Concentration name: Advanced Building Systems (ABS), Building Performance and Diagnostics (BPD), and Computational Design (CD)
description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Architecture is a research-based degree program that prepares students for careers in research, teaching, and advanced professional practice. The program’s mission is to be at the forefront of the discipline by defining and developing the discipline’s most advanced knowledge and methods. The Ph.D. program leverages the School of Architecture's strengths to cultivate a select number of students to become the next generation of leaders in architecture and building science. The program’s strength resides in its interdisciplinary approach to research and its situation within a premier technological university. The Ph.D. in Architecture program has three tracks: Advanced Building Systems (ABS), Building Performance and Diagnostics (BPD), and Computational Design (CD).

The Ph.D. in Building Performance and Diagnostics (BPD) educates students to become experts in the scientific research of high-performance buildings. Students learn to apply fundamental principles of building science to develop and deploy innovative technologies and integrated design solutions to radically improve the performance of new and existing buildings. We focus on four core areas of building performance: Building Physics; Advanced Building Systems Integration and Controls; Computational Design Support; and Building-related Occupant Behavior, Health, and Comfort. Our program addresses major national and global challenges including the large energy and environmental footprints of buildings, and the growing demand for healthy and productive indoor environments. The program is tailored to the individual professional and research interests of each student. Each plan of study includes a set of required courses and a broad range of electives that may be taken in the School of Architecture, as well as in other departments at Carnegie Mellon. Graduates of the Ph.D.-BPD program are prepared to pursue academic careers in leading national and international universities or as research scientists in national labs and advanced industrial research and development centers. Learn more about the BPD PhD program in the SoA Graduate Programs Student Handbook.
Program name: Ph.D. in Building Performance and Diagnostics

description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Computational Design (PhD in CD) is a post-professional research-based degree program that trains students to develop and apply novel computational methods to address complex challenges in the built environment. Our interdisciplinary research community develops new knowledge in a range of research areas, including: generative and parametric design, building performance simulation, building information modeling (BIM), design cognition, human-computer interaction, interactive and responsive environments, design machine learning, robotic fabrication, and computational making. We draw on a diverse array of computational techniques, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, sensing and actuation, optimization, and human-computer interaction. The program aims to place graduates in high-level research careers in academia, industry, and government. The PhD in CD program seeks applicants with strong design, technical and/or programming backgrounds, from a variety of fields including architecture, engineering, computer science, and industrial design.

The Master of Fine Arts degree is a three-year, interdisciplinary, studio-based program. Students are supported in developing a sustainable and challenging art practice. The School of Art facilitates this development through a curriculum that includes rigorous studio and research advising with core faculty, critiques with visiting artists and critics, cohort-driven seminars, and skill-based workshops. Elective coursework is strongly encouraged and allows graduate students to take advantage of the diverse academic offerings across the university.

Concentration name: design for digital and physical products
description: The two-year Master of Design (MDes) program is for students with an undergraduate degree in design or a related field. The program focuses on design for interactions and services. Students choose a focus area that aligns with their professional and academic goals. Current focus areas include design for social innovation, design for service and design for digital and physical products. Students can also pursue a self-defined focus. The School of Design also offers a one-year Master of Professional Studies (MPS) program for students who have at least three years of professional experience post-baccalaureate and a two-year Master of Arts in Design (MA) program for students with an undergraduate degree in an area other than design.

The PhD in Design at Carnegie Mellon is for students with a master's degree in design or a related field who are interested in a career in research and teaching. Our program offers a unique, research-based course of study for a small and select group of students from around the world. PhD students work with faculty on a wide range of design research projects. Recent dissertation topics include a study of gender and domestic product design, the role of design in corporate strategy, and the history of corporate identity in the United States. Many of our PhD graduates now hold tenure-track faculty positions in prominent design programs in the United States and abroad. Our PhD program focuses primarily on research that deepens our understanding of design practice and pedagogy. We do not support research focused on designing new products, services, or design methods, except where these are components of a larger research project about design. Instead, we encourage research that addresses design from a number of perspectives, including historical, theoretical, and methodological.

The Master of Fine Arts programs prepare students for professional careers in the theater and entertainment industry. The primary pedagogical goal is the development of the theater artist. This is achieved through a conservatory approach to training within the context of a research university. The curriculum is carefully structured and sequenced. The production program offers a range of theatrical genres and styles providing a variety of practical experiences that challenge and extend the student’s developing skills and aesthetic. Each program focuses on collaboration as an essential skill for the contemporary theater artist. The Master of Fine Arts degree is offered in Directing, Dramatic Writing, Dramaturgy, and Design (scenic, costume, lighting, and sound) and Production (production technology and management).
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Drama

description: The School of Drama's PhD in Drama offers a unique opportunity for students to pursue a rigorous academic course of study at a top-tier research university situated within one of the nation's oldest and most respected conservatory programs. The course of study is interdisciplinary, combining history/theory/criticism with performance and dramaturgy, and it capitalizes on the rich intellectual and artistic resources of the School of Drama, the College of Fine Arts, and Carnegie Mellon University. Students work closely with faculty in the School of Drama and across the university. The program is intentionally small, allowing for flexibility in the student's program of study and a great deal of individual mentorship. The PhD in Drama prepares students to be the next generation of leading scholar/artists in the field.

The Master of Music program is a two-year course of study for students who hold the bachelor's degree and who have demonstrated a high level of potential for a professional career in music. The degree provides an opportunity for students to develop their major field to the highest professional standards, while at the same time broadening their knowledge of all aspects of music, the humanities and the sciences. The degree is granted in the fields of performance (instrumental, vocal and keyboard), composition and conducting.
Accreditation status: Carnegie Mellon University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: The Carnegie Mellon School of Music doctoral program is a small, focused course of study that offers a Ph.D. in music. Students select from three areas of specialization: musicology, composition, or theory. The program encourages interdisciplinary work with other departments at Carnegie Mellon, as well as cross-registration through the Pittsburgh Council on Higher Education (PCHE). The Ph.D. in Music is a residential program that requires full-time study.
Accreditation status: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: The Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (MSAIE) is a professional master's degree program that develops students’ skills in applying artificial intelligence to a wide variety of practical problems. MSAIE students learn to design and build AI systems that are secure, ethical, and responsible. The program culminates in a capstone project in which students apply what they have learned to a practical, real-world problem. Graduates of the MSAIE program will have the skills and knowledge to serve as AI engineers, data scientists, and AI research scientists in government, industry, and the non-profit sector. The MSAIE degree can be completed in three semesters of full-time study. Students may elect to complete an optional practical training experience in the summer between their second and third semesters. With the practical training option, the program takes 16 months to complete.
Program name: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering - CARNEGIE MELLON INSTITUTE FOR STRATEGY AND TECHNOLOGY

description: The program in Neural Computation and Engineering (NCE) is a new cross-college Ph.D. program offered by the Neuroscience Institute in collaboration with multiple departments across Carnegie Mellon. The NCE program builds upon CMU’s historical strengths in computation and neuroscience to provide a unique training program that gives students a deep understanding of both the brain and computation. Students receive training in neuroscience, data science, machine learning, and computational modeling, with the ultimate goal being to train the next generation of researchers who can bridge the gap between these fields. Our curriculum is tailored to students from a variety of backgrounds including biology, neuroscience, psychology, computer science, engineering, and physics. Students participate in core courses in neuroscience, computation and data science, and engage in cross-disciplinary research that develops and leverages these skills to understand the brain. Training emphasizes the development of computational tools for analyzing large-scale neural and behavioral datasets and for modeling complex neural systems.
Program name: Ph.D. in Neural Computation and Engineering

description: The Master of Arts in Professional Writing (MAPW) program is a one-year, two-semester program for students who want to become professional writers, editors, and communication specialists. The program focuses on teaching students the rhetorical principles and practices necessary for success as a professional writer in a variety of fields, including business, science and technology, government, and non-profit organizations. It prepares students for a variety of careers through a flexible curriculum that can be tailored to individual students' needs and interests. The program requires 90 units of coursework. In addition to a variety of courses in writing and communication, students can also take courses in other departments at Carnegie Mellon, as well as complete an internship or a master's thesis.
Program name: Master of Arts in Professional Writing

description: The M.A. in Rhetoric is a one-year (two-semester), full-time, residential program for students seeking a terminal master’s degree in rhetoric. The program provides a strong foundation in rhetorical history, theory, and criticism, while also providing opportunities for students to develop their own interests in specialized areas of research. The curriculum gives students experience with a variety of research methods and theoretical perspectives as they prepare to do their own scholarly work in the field. Students work closely with faculty, and are well-supported in their professional goals, whether they aim to go on to Ph.D. programs in rhetoric or a related field, or to pursue careers in which advanced training in communication and analysis is highly valued. The M.A. in Rhetoric degree requires 72 units of coursework, usually fulfilled by taking three graduate courses per semester for two semesters. A required course, 76-701 Introduction to Rhetorical Theory, is offered in the fall. An M.A. Thesis (76-800) is also required. Other courses are chosen from the graduate seminars regularly offered by rhetoric faculty.

The graduate program in Rhetoric at Carnegie Mellon is a Ph.D. program that prepares students for research and teaching in universities and for research in the private and public sectors. We view rhetoric as the study of how language and other symbolic systems are used to create, maintain, and transform our social worlds. We are interested in how people communicate, why they communicate in the particular ways that they do, how they learned to do so, and how their communication might be improved. In exploring these questions we have focused on a wide range of written, oral, and visual texts, from scientific and technical articles to public policy debates, from courtroom arguments to online discussion groups. Research in rhetoric at Carnegie Mellon is problem-driven, eclectic in method, and interdisciplinary. The program takes advantage of the university's strengths in technology, communication, and interdisciplinary research. Further information about the program may be found at the Department of English World Wide Web server.

Concentration name: History of Science, Technology, and the Environment
description:
The graduate program in history at Carnegie Mellon is small, selective, and innovative. We are best known for our interdisciplinary approach to historical studies and our focus on the historical roots of contemporary social, political, and economic problems. Our program is organized into three broad fields of study: Social and Cultural History, Global History, and the History of Science, Technology, and the Environment. Although there are many areas of overlap and connection between these fields, all students will select a major field in one of these three areas and develop two minor fields in consultation with their advisors. Students will also be expected to achieve competence in a foreign language or in statistical or other advanced methodologies.

The doctoral program generally requires five years of full-time study. Students take courses during their first two years to prepare them for qualifying exams, which are generally taken at the end of the second year. Upon passing the qualifying exams, students advance to candidacy and begin work on their dissertations. Throughout their careers, students work closely with their advisors, who help them to prepare for their exams and develop their dissertation topics. All Ph.D. students are fully funded for five years. Funding packages include a tuition waiver, a generous stipend, and a health insurance subsidy.

The M.A. in Global Communication and Applied Translation (GCAT) is a one-year, two-semester program for students who have advanced abilities in at least one language other than English (e.g., Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Spanish) and an interest in translation, localization, and global communication. The program focuses on translation technologies and project management for the localization industry. The program can be completed in two semesters of full-time study. GCAT is an excellent option for those who wish to pursue a career as a translator or localization project manager, as well as for those who wish to teach translation or pursue doctoral study in translation.
Program name: Master of Arts in Global Communication and Applied Translation

description: The M.A. program in Second Language Acquisition (SLA) has a strong interdisciplinary focus. Its primary goal is to provide graduate students with a solid foundation in the key areas of linguistic theory, second language acquisition theory, and research methodology. Building on this foundation, students can focus on one or more areas of second language studies including the role of individual differences in second language learning, technology-enhanced language learning, classroom-based second language research, second language literacy, and second/foreign language pedagogy. The program is designed to prepare students for two main career tracks: 1. to enter a doctoral program in SLA or a related field; 2. to obtain a professional position as a foreign/second language specialist in a variety of national or international settings in the public or private sector.
Program name: Master of Arts in Second Language Acquisition

description: The Ph.D. in Second Language Acquisition is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the acquisition of second languages in both instructed and naturalistic settings. This empirically-driven program provides a strong foundation in theories of second language acquisition, research methodology, and the cognitive and neurological bases of bilingualism. Students in the program develop expertise in an area of specialization such as language program administration, technology-enhanced learning, classroom-based research, heritage language learning, sociolinguistics, or psycholinguistics. The program is committed to a mentorship model in which students work closely with faculty members on research projects. This research training prepares students for careers as faculty members in academic departments (e.g., Modern Languages, Second Language Studies, Applied Linguistics, English/ESL, Education) or as language specialists in government, the private sector, and non-profit organizations.

The Ph.D. program in Philosophy is a research-oriented program designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. The Department of Philosophy at Carnegie Mellon is a world leader in a variety of research areas, including logic, philosophy of science, philosophy of language, philosophy of mind, formal epistemology, and ethics. The graduate program is a small and focused program in which students and faculty have the opportunity for regular and close interaction. All graduate students receive five years of funding, and they are offered ample opportunities for teaching and teaching preparation.

The Department of Psychology offers a program leading to the Ph.D. degree that is distinguished by its focus on psychological science. The department does not offer a clinical training program. The graduate program focuses on a number of areas including cognitive psychology, cognitive neuroscience, developmental psychology, educational psychology, and social/personality/health psychology. Students in each of these areas are encouraged to develop a program of courses and research that meets their own specific interests, taking advantage of the unique strengths available within the department and, more broadly, within the university. The program is designed to be completed in five years. All students are admitted for the fall semester.

The Ph.D. program in social and decision sciences is a research-based program that trains students in the tradition of the "Carnegie School" to conduct research on problems of theory and application that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries. Students take core courses in the fields that form the foundations of decision sciences—cognitive psychology, social psychology, organizational behavior, economics, political science and statistics—and then specialize in one or more of these areas. In addition to our core faculty, students have access to the broad range of faculty talent available at Carnegie Mellon. The program is small, selective and informal, and is characterized by close work between students and faculty. The program prepares students primarily for academic careers in universities and research institutions.
Program name: Ph.D. in Social and Decision Sciences

description: The Ph.D. program in the Department of Statistics & Data Science at Carnegie Mellon University is arguably the premier doctoral program in the world for statistics. We train students to become researchers and leaders in the field of statistics and data science, both in academia and in industry. The training is a mix of core statistical theory and methodology, and a wide variety of specialty topics. Our Ph.D. students take courses from and conduct research with our world-renowned faculty, developing expertise in areas such as theory and foundations of statistics and probability, statistical methodology, computational statistics, interdisciplinary research, and statistical practice.
Program name: Ph.D. in Statistics and Data Science

description: The Master of Arts Management (M.A.M.) program prepares students to lead and manage arts and cultural organizations through a combination of rigorous coursework in management, data analysis, technology, and experiential learning. The two-year program is joint between the Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy and the College of Fine Arts. The curriculum is designed to give students a deep understanding of the arts and cultural landscape, as well as the practical skills needed to succeed in a variety of roles in the field. Students learn from faculty who are experts in their fields, and they have the opportunity to work with leading arts and cultural organizations in Pittsburgh and around the world. The M.A.M. program is committed to preparing students for leadership roles in the arts and cultural sector, and to fostering a more equitable and sustainable future for the arts.

Carnegie Mellon University's Master of Entertainment Industry Management (MEIM) program is the best in the world at preparing students to be the next generation of leaders in the business of film, television, music, theater, and interactive media. Our graduates are more than just managers—they are creative executives with the analytical skills to solve problems and the finesse to excel in the complex, ever-changing entertainment landscape. In the MEIM program, you will gain a deep understanding of the entertainment industry, its structures, and its business practices. The program consists of a year of classes at Carnegie Mellon's Pittsburgh campus followed by a year of classes and a required, full-time internship in Los Angeles at CMU's Heinz College LA center.

Concentration name: Health Care Analytics, Health Care Management
